changes: The auction page opens the complete FRED source artifact on demand. All seventeen existing requests, received/unavailable/not-requested states, units, full returned and selected row counts, observation ranges, acquisition clocks and warm-cache reuse are visible together.

Typed content-addressed references reject external/private paths. Bounded response reading, exact length and SHA-256 checks precede parsing. The browser independently checks source coverage, acquisition metadata, row normalization, exclusions, duplicate/future dates, selected histories and row counts. This is input inspection, not a replay of the full auction model.

The full field inspector retains access to every original parsed response and calculation input. Missing data never becomes zero. Complete capture is separate from measurement availability, and all forecast/Calls/sizing/execution qualification flags must remain false.

The policy-rate headline now requires a matching finite DFF trace and prints its observation date. Missing, stale, inconsistent or mismatched traces withhold the headline; true zero remains 0.00. A missing or cached older viewer API does not crash the page.

Failed inspection clears previous content and remains retryable. A changed or stale publication aborts outstanding work and prevents its result from repainting the page. No source artifact is automatically downloaded.

The responsive table preserves all seventeen rows with a sticky series column, keyboard-focusable horizontal scrolling, visible focus styling and explicit scrolling instructions. Cache versions bind the updated main renderer and source viewer.
limitations: Browser acceptance uses isolated synthetic full artifacts generated by the actual reviewed Python producer. It does not certify live current packets, provider definitions or first-release historical availability.

The backend is unchanged and already accepted at its separate source commit. Normal publication of its new archive remains pending the original 13:05 UTC schedule; no manual native invocation, extra provider request or cadence change is made.
The browser checks exact retained measurements and row selections. It does not refetch raw provider bodies or replay the full legacy auction scoring/analog/issuance model.
Portfolio sizing, forecast edge, independent validation, peak native capacity and the remaining platform workstreams remain open.
